specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** local-reviewer-scope-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight tasks belongs to the local reviewer role or must be referred to someone else, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Local Reviewer Role, Certificate, Submission Review (all defined in this chapter above this block), and the privacy section of Chapter 13. **Evidence of Mastery:** For each task the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the role description is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A certified teacher can rule on what is legal. (2) A local reviewer approves adoptions alone. (3) Certifying others is part of the role. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging the boundary of a role is an Evaluate-level action that protects both the reviewer and the colleagues who rely on them. Tasks that look similar to in-role tasks but fall outside teach the learner where to refer. **Content:** The two bins: In the role, and Refer or do not do. The eight tasks (all made up): | # | Task | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Score a colleague's quiz with the rubric and an agent, and verify the agent's claims. | In the role | It is the core of the role. | | 2 | Keep a findings log for each review. | In the role | The log is part of the method. | | 3 | Tell a colleague which metric to fix first. | In the role | It applies the lowest-metric-first rule. | | 4 | Decide that a resource's license is legally safe to publish. | Refer or do not do | Legal questions go to the school's counsel or privacy officer. | | 5 | Send a class roster with student names to the agent. | Refer or do not do | Student information stays out of prompts. | | 6 | Approve a district-wide adoption on their own. | Refer or do not do | Adoption follows the school's own process. | | 7 | Repeat the calibration exercise on a reference set once a year. | In the role | It keeps the reviewer accurate. | | 8 | Certify another teacher. | Refer or do not do | Certification belongs to the program's reviewers. | **Provenance:** The tasks are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The scope follows the chapter section "Local Reviewer Role" and Chapters 11, 13, and 14. **Rules:** Each task has exactly one correct bin, four per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one task and the two bins. 2. The learner places the task in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After task 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 tasks in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This task is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You know where the role ends." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed task. **Starting State:** The first task in the shuffled order and the two bins. The question shown is "Is this part of the local reviewer's job?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists four limits of the role: no legal rulings, no student information in prompts, no solo adoption decisions, and no certifying of others.
